events.title: Crusaders Process Around Jerusalem
events.description: About 15,000 starving Christian soldiers of the First Crusade walked in a religious procession around the walls of Jerusalem. Its Muslim defenders watched from the ramparts.
events.significance: The procession came days before the crusaders' final assault. The city fell on July 15, 1099, a turning point of the First Crusade.

events.title: Vasco da Gama Sets Sail for India
events.description: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama left Lisbon with four ships on the first direct European voyage to India.
events.significance: The voyage opened a sea route between Europe and Asia. It reshaped global trade and helped build Portugal's maritime empire.

events.title: Declaration of Independence Read Publicly
events.description: The Declaration of Independence received its first formal public reading in Philadelphia, and the Liberty Bell was rung.
events.significance: The reading brought the case for American independence to ordinary citizens. It helped rally support for the new nation.

events.title: The Wall Street Journal Debuts
events.description: The first issue of The Wall Street Journal was published in New York.
events.significance: The paper became one of the world's most widely circulated business dailies. It shaped how financial news is reported.

events.title: Roswell UFO Reports Spread
events.description: News reports went out that a UFO had crash-landed near Roswell, New Mexico.
events.significance: The story grew into one of the best-known UFO legends. It has influenced popular culture for decades.
